### aws-cli-credential-precedence-command-line-env-then-files

**Claim.** CLI settings take precedence in a fixed order: command line options first, then environment variables, then assumed roles, IAM Identity Center, the credentials file, a custom process, the config file, container credentials and finally EC2 instance profile credentials.

**Write it as.** `Command line options` · `Environment variables` · `Credentials file` · `Amazon EC2 instance profile credentials`

> "Certain authentication take precedence over others. The AWS CLI authentication settings take precedence in the following order:"
> — [Authentication and access credentials for the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-authentication.html)

> "**Command line options** – Overrides settings in any other location, such as the `--region`, `--output`, and `--profile` parameters."
> — [Authentication and access credentials for the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-authentication.html)

> "**Environment variables** – You can store values in your system's environment variables."
> — [Authentication and access credentials for the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-authentication.html)

> "**Credentials file** – The `credentials` and `config` file are updated when you run the command `aws configure`. The `credentials` file is located at `~/.aws/credentials` on Linux or macOS, or at `C:\Users\{{USERNAME}}\.aws\credentials` on Windows."
> — [Authentication and access credentials for the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-authentication.html)

> "**Amazon EC2 instance profile credentials** – You can associate an IAM role with each of your Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances. Temporary credentials for that role are then available to code running in the instance. The credentials are delivered through the Amazon EC2 metadata service."
> — [Authentication and access credentials for the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-chap-authentication.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-11.

### aws-cli-credentials-and-config-files-in-dot-aws

**Claim.** The AWS CLI stores the credentials you enter with aws configure in a file named credentials, and the less sensitive settings in a file named config, both in the .aws folder in your home directory.

**Write it as.** `.aws folder in your home directory`

**Scope.** AWS CLI configuration.

> "The AWS CLI stores sensitive credential information that you specify with `aws configure` in a local file named `credentials`, in a folder named `.aws` in your home directory. > — [Configuration and credential file settings in the AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-11.
